taxAppealStigmaRelief.legalDoctrine: Under New Jersey Tax Court precedent (Glen Wall Associates v. Wall Twp), properties burdened by periodic flooding, high water tables, or severe stormwater easement restrictions suffer from permanent market stigma. Because willing buyers discount properties with mandatory $2,000–$4,000/year flood insurance premiums, assessments that do not reflect this penalty violate the uniform assessment clause of the NJ Constitution.

appealChecklistPassaicCounty: 1. Obtain Official FEMA FIRMette map showing property parcel inside Zone AE or Zone X500 from msc.fema.gov.
2. Provide FEMA Elevation Certificate (Form 086-0-33) certified by licensed NJ Land Surveyor.
3. Submit Copy of Flood Insurance Policy Declaration Page proving annual premium cost (e.g. $3,200/yr).
4. Submit Dated Photographs of storm inundation water lines or sump pump remediation invoices.
5. Provide 3–5 comparable non-flood sales within Clifton sold during the qualifying calendar year, demonstrating the price premium dry homes command over flood-impacted parcels.
6. File Passaic County Board of Taxation Form A-1 prior to April 1 statutory deadline.
